page: Microsoft Azure D64ds_v6 is a general-purpose virtual machine based on the x86_64 architecture, managed by Microsoft Hyper-V. It is powered by an Intel Xeon 8573C processor running at 4.2 GHz, providing 64 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 32 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. Cache configuration includes 48 KB of L1 data cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and a large 260 MB L3 cache pool. The processor supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512, AMX (Tile and INT8), VAES, and SHA-NI.

The system is equipped with 256.0 GB of memory, preserving a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio at 4.0 GB per vCPU. Storage architecture features 3,780 GB of integrated local NVMe SSD capacity alongside support for Azure Premium Storage. The instance does not include integrated GPU accelerators. Network provisioning includes zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses, requiring standard virtual network configuration for external connectivity.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong compute and throughput capabilities. Geekbench scores reach 2,011.0 for single-core and 17,892.0 for multi-core performance, supported by an aggregate PassMark CPU score of 67,787.17. High vector and integer performance is evident in software compilation (43,716.0) and ray tracing (66,597.0). Multi-threaded bzip3 decompression reaches 341.2 GB/sec, while static web serving throughput places in the top tier at 94.85 GB/sec.

Memory-intensive tests reveal certain tradeoffs. While cached small-block memory reads achieve 4,212.73 GB/sec, uncached large-block transfers drop to 149.32 GB/sec for reads and 69.85 GB/sec for writes, resulting in a weak PassMark memory score of 1,581.88. In contrast, database and caching benchmarks remain strong, with PassMark database operations at 24,055.67 and Redis throughput sustaining 75.07 million SET operations per second.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the D64ds_v6 combines dedicated compute density, hardware AMX acceleration, and fast local NVMe storage into a single enterprise instance without the premium overhead of dedicated GPU resources. These hardware traits make the instance suitable for large-scale static web serving, enterprise databases, caching layers, software compilation clusters, and CPU-based LLM inference tasks.
description: Microsoft Azure D64ds_v6 is a general-purpose virtual machine equipped with 64 dedicated vCPUs across 32 physical cores, driven by an Intel Xeon 8573C processor running at up to 4.2 GHz. The system provides 256.0 GB of RAM alongside 3,780 GB of fast local NVMe SSD storage, though it lacks discrete GPU acceleration. Benefiting from hardware support for AMX and AVX-512 instruction sets, the server demonstrates strong compute throughput, excelling in software compilation, Redis key-value workloads (75.07 million operations per second), and top-tier static web serving throughput (94.85 GB/sec). Although large uncached memory block bandwidth exhibits average performance, the combination of substantial multi-core processing power and high-speed local NVMe storage makes it well suited for enterprise database hosting, large web application layers, continuous integration build nodes, and mid-sized CPU-driven LLM inference pipelines.
